examples.en: Our school festival was a huge success.
The new product was a big hit, so the factory got busy.
I think this movie will be a big hit.
For a new shop to be a great success, service is important.
The presentation went great, so the team leader praised us.
Even a hugely successful singer was unknown at first.

explain: 결과를 말할 때 '-했어요'로 자주 써요. 구어체로는 '대박 나다'도 많이 써서 '영화가 대박 났어요'라고 해요. 사람에게는 '크게 성공하다'가 더 부드러워요.

phrases.example: 그 가게는 새 메뉴가 대박 났어요.
phrases.en: That shop's new menu was a big hit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구어체로 많이 써요. 친구와 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A colloquial expression, natural in casual talk.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 사업을 시작해서 크게 성공했어요.
phrases.en: That friend started a business and succeeded greatly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 쓸 때 더 부드럽고 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, more natural choice when talking about people.

phrases.en: I hope tomorrow's show will be a huge success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바라는 마음을 말할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to express a wish.
phrases.en_equiv: I hope it's a great success

explain_en: It is often used in the past tense, '-했어요', to report a result. In casual speech '대박 나다' is also very common, as in '영화가 대박 났어요'. For a person, '크게 성공하다' sounds softer.

examples.en: This festival was a huge success.
I heard the opening ceremony was a great success.
I'm glad the school bazaar ended as a big success.
The newly opened restaurant has been packed since day one.

examples.ko: 사람이 많이 와서 행사는 대성황 속에 끝났어요.
examples.en: Lots of people came, and the event ended in great success.

examples.ko: 대성황 덕분에 다음 행사도 열기로 했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the great turnout, we decided to hold the next event too.

explain: 행사, 공연, 가게에 사람이 많이 모여서 크게 잘되었을 때 써요. '대성황을 이루다', '대성황을 이루었다'로 많이 말해요. 구어로는 '대박'이라고도 하지만 '대성황'은 조금 격식 있게 들려요.

phrases.en: Today's performance was a great success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical collocation.

phrases.en: Yesterday's bazaar was a real smash hit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 끝난 뒤 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the result after an event.

phrases.en: The newly opened bakery is a huge hit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구어체이고 '대성황'보다 가볍고 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Colloquial, lighter and more casual than 대성황.

explain_en: Use it when an event, show, or shop draws a big crowd and goes very well. It is common as '대성황을 이루다'. Casually people say '대박', but '대성황' sounds somewhat more formal.

examples.en: If you inhale slowly, your mind relaxes.
In yoga, inhaling and exhaling are very important.

examples.ko: 들숨에 배를 내밀고 날숨에 넣어 보세요.
examples.en: Push your belly out as you inhale and pull it in as you exhale.
If your inhale is short, you run out of breath quickly.
Breathe in through your nose and out through your mouth.

examples.ko: 들숨보다 날숨을 길게 쉬면 긴장이 풀려요.
examples.en: If you breathe out longer than you breathe in, tension eases.

explain: 반대말은 '날숨'이고, 호흡 운동이나 명상, 노래 수업 같은 설명에서 자주 나와요. 평소 대화에서는 '숨을 들이쉬다'와 '숨을 내쉬다'라고 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Try breathing in and out slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '날숨'과 함께 묶어서 쓰는 경우가 가장 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used together with its opposite, '날숨'.

phrases.en: Close your eyes and take a deep breath in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '들숨' 대신 이 표현을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This phrase is used more than '들숨' in everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 깊은 들숨 뒤에 숨을 잠깐 멈추세요.
phrases.en: After a deep inhale, hold your breath for a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깊은'을 붙여서 숨을 크게 들이쉬는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '깊은' describes taking a big breath in.

explain_en: Its opposite is '날숨', and it often appears in explanations for breathing exercises, meditation and singing lessons. In everyday talk people more often say '숨을 들이쉬다' and '숨을 내쉬다'.

examples.en: You have to enter a string in this field.
I learned how to count the length of a string.
I saved it as a string, not as a number.
If the string is too long, an error occurs.

examples.ko: 이 함수는 글자를 거꾸로 바꾸는 문자열 처리를 해요.
examples.en: This function does string processing that reverses the characters.

examples.ko: 빈 문자열은 아무 글자도 없는 값이에요.
examples.en: An empty string is a value with no characters at all.

explain: 프로그래밍에서 숫자와 구별해서 글자를 이어 놓은 값을 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 '문자열 처리', '문자열 길이'처럼 컴퓨터 이야기에서 나와요.

phrases.en: Enter a string in the search box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터에 글자를 이어서 넣을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for typing characters in a row into a computer.

phrases.en: If there are no characters at all, it's an empty string.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자가 하나도 없는 문자열을 말해요. 프로그래밍 수업에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A string with no characters; often appears in programming lessons.

phrases.en: This code converts a string into a number.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자로 된 값을 다른 형태로 바꾸는 작업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for turning a text value into another form.

explain_en: In programming it is used to separate a run of characters from a number. It almost never appears in daily talk; you see it in computer topics like 'string processing' or 'string length'.

examples.en: This video is not suitable for elementary school students.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 본 영상물이 아주 인상적이었어요.
examples.en: The video we watched in class was very impressive.
You can borrow videos from the library.
You must not upload illegal videos.

examples.ko: 영상물 등급에 따라 볼 수 있는 나이가 달라요.
examples.en: The age you need to be to watch differs by video rating.
Our company makes educational videos.

explain: 영화, 드라마, 유튜브 영상을 한꺼번에 가리킬 때 쓰는 말로 법, 공문, 학교 이야기에서 자주 보여요. 친구와 말할 때는 그냥 '영상'이나 '동영상'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: A friend sent me a funny video.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영상물'은 공식적인 말이고, 친구와 말할 때는 '동영상'을 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '영상물' is formal; in everyday talk with friends people usually say '동영상'.

phrases.en: I checked the video rating and chose a movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이에 맞는 영화나 드라마를 구분하는 등급을 말할 때 자주 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the age rating that decides who can watch a film or drama.

phrases.en: The teacher showed us an educational video.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 수업에서 쓰는 영상을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for videos used in school or lessons.

explain_en: It covers films, dramas and online videos all at once and shows up in laws, official documents and school settings. When chatting with friends, people just say '영상' or '동영상'.

examples.en: The audience responds enthusiastically to the song.
The students responded well to the teacher's questions.

examples.ko: 손님들이 호응해 주면 가게 주인은 힘이 나요.
examples.en: When customers respond warmly, the shop owner feels energized.

examples.ko: 이 광고에 젊은 사람들이 크게 호응하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Young people seem to respond enthusiastically to this ad.
I offered an idea, but nobody responded to it.
Is there anyone who will go along with the company's proposal?

explain: 누군가의 말이나 행동에 좋은 쪽으로 반응해서 같이 움직인다는 느낌이에요. '호응이 좋다', '호응을 얻다'처럼 명사로도 자주 써요. 그냥 답을 하는 '대답하다'와 달리 관심과 동의가 담겨 있어요.

phrases.example: 새 광고가 사람들에게 큰 호응을 얻었어요.
phrases.en: The new ad got a great response from people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 좋게 반응해 줬다는 뜻으로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly means that people responded to something favorably.

phrases.en: The audience responded well to this performance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반응이 뜨겁고 긍정적일 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for when the reaction is warm and positive.

phrases.example: 팬들이 가수의 말에 크게 호응해 줬어요.
phrases.en: The fans responded warmly to the singer's words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 말이나 행동에 맞춰 같이 움직여 준다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of joining in with what another person says or does.

explain_en: It carries the feeling of reacting positively and moving along with someone's words or actions. You also see the noun forms, as in '호응이 좋다' and '호응을 얻다'. Unlike 대답하다 (just giving an answer), it implies interest and agreement.

examples.en: The teacher called the students with a loudspeaker.
The candidate greeted people holding a megaphone.
The playground is big, so we need a loudspeaker.

examples.ko: 확성기 소리가 너무 커서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The loudspeaker was so loud that I was startled.

examples.ko: 저 확성기는 고장이 났는지 소리가 끊겨요.
examples.en: That loudspeaker seems broken because the sound keeps cutting out.

examples.ko: 축제 때 확성기에서 신나는 음악이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Upbeat music came out of the loudspeaker during the festival.

explain: 소리를 크게 키워서 멀리까지 들리게 하는 장치예요. 학교 운동장, 선거 유세, 축제처럼 넓은 곳에서 쓰고, 손에 들고 쓰는 것은 '메가폰'이라고도 해요. '스피커'는 컴퓨터나 오디오에서 소리가 나오는 장치를 가리키는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: The police spoke to the crowd through a loudspeaker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓은 곳에서 크게 알릴 때 '확성기로'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 확성기로 when announcing loudly in a wide space.

phrases.en: The head cheerleader cheered while holding a megaphone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손에 들고 쓰는 확성기를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the hand-held kind of loudspeaker.

phrases.en: The loudspeaker sound outside is too loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확성기에서 나오는 큰 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the loud sound coming from a loudspeaker.

explain_en: It is a device that makes sound louder so it carries far. It is used in wide places such as school playgrounds, election campaigns and festivals, and the hand-held kind is also called a '메가폰'. '스피커' more often refers to the part of a computer or audio system that outputs sound.

examples.en: When is this shop usually closed?

examples.ko: 이번 달 휴무일은 달력에 따로 표시해 두었어요.
examples.en: I marked this month's days off separately on the calendar.

examples.ko: 매주 월요일이 휴무일이라서 미리 전화해 봤어요.
examples.en: Mondays are the weekly day off, so I called ahead.

examples.ko: 도서관 휴무일에는 책을 반납할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't return books on the library's closed days.

examples.ko: 공휴일이 휴무일과 겹쳐서 하루 더 쉬어요.
examples.en: The public holiday overlaps with the closed day, so we get one more day off.

examples.ko: 휴무일을 확인하지 않고 갔다가 그냥 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: I went without checking the closed day and just came back.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '쉬는 날'이라고 하고, '휴무일'은 가게·병원·도서관의 안내문에서 자주 보여요. '정기 휴무일'처럼 정해진 날을 말할 때도 많이 써요. 반대로 문을 여는 날은 '영업일'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Tomorrow is the shop's day off.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴무일'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more casual, everyday way to say '휴무일'.

phrases.en: This restaurant's regular closed day is Monday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매주 또는 매달 정해진 날에 쉴 때 쓰고, 가게 안내문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a fixed weekly or monthly closing day, often seen on shop notices.

phrases.en: We don't answer the phone on closed days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴무일'에 조사 '에는'을 붙여 그날에 하는 일이나 규칙을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the particle '에는' to talk about rules or things that happen on a closed day.

explain_en: In everyday talk people say '쉬는 날', while '휴무일' often appears on notices for shops, clinics and libraries. It is also used in '정기 휴무일' (regular closing day). The opposite, a day when a place is open, is '영업일'.
